posts.cooked:
Defeat Advanced Baron Blade in Megalopolis, using only heros who are not members of any usual teams.

Challenge Complete! 

Baron Blade knew victory was at hand.  Cooperation is what made the heroes so strong, but thanks to his plans all the heroes with cooperative experience were elsewhere.  Individually the one who stood before him were powerful, but they knew nothing of teamwork.
 
It was true that Chrono-Ranger, Guise, KNYFE, The Naturalist, and Ra were not the most friendly of folks.  They tended to irritate people they spent time with, and the other members of this irregular band were no execption.  But they could all agree on one thing:  Baron Blade was going down, and he was going down hard!
 
 
This actually took me three tries.  The first try went marvelously, but I forgot to challenge him Advanced, so it didn't count.  In the second try, we were gearing up to flip him when the baron made us Consider the Price of Victory during a Hostage Situation, and we didn't have enough damage on the board to flip him.  In the third game, By Any Means + Imbued Fire and Uh, Yeah, I'm That Guy boosted our power so high that it cut through Blade's Living Force Field and his Power Armor, and he was dead in no time at all.

posts.cooked:
Traitor Sentinels, the Sentinels Traitor Game!

Word had come in, Haka was awake, and while he couldn't talk, he was able to get a message through, "save her".

The Freedom 4 had never seen Haka like this, Fanatic and Tempest where nowhere to be found.  Maia was able to track their movements, it seemed that Haka, Tempest and Fanatic had travelled to Atlantis.  Captain Cosmic and The Argent Adept were still involved in negotiations off world, and could not be reached.

"This is it team, we don't know what we are facing down there, but our friends are in trouble, and we are going in."  The Freedom 4 was ready for anything, or so they thought.

Upon arriving at the underwater ruins they were greeted by a familiar face, Helena seemed a bit off, but was inviting, and assured them that Tempest was okay, but when she led them to him, they found him in chains, wierdly runed devices causing him pain.

"What is going on here?" Legacy asked.

"Let the master explain," Fanatic answered.

"Yes, let me explain," came the voice of Bezeliel, the demon known as Apostate.

"Well, now we know what happened." Wraith said matter of factly.  

"We're going to pass on that explanation," Tachyon yelled as she zoomed towards Tempest.

 

Apostate in Ruins of Atlantis vs. F5 LEgacy, Wraith, (traitor) X-treme Prime Warden Fanatic, Super Scientific Tachyon, and GI Bunker.

 

I thought this would be a lot harder than it was, F5 Legacy started with 2 Bolster Allies and by turn 3 got the third one.  We got amazing cards and shut down Apostate.  Fanatic got 2 chastise, which were immediately destroyed by Tachyon (chastise on orb is not cool) and Martyr, and got to use Smite twice.  Hypersonic Assault and Throat Jab crushed Apostate's damage while 2 Kraken and Panzer Buster took care of all the relics.

Once Legacy got Superhuman/Fortitude/lead (I was counting Fanatic as a villain target because otherwise things broke) the danger was pretty much over.

Final health:  Legacy 22, Wraith 18, Fanatic 22, Tachyon 15 and Bunker 17

It was an unlikely…perhaps one should really say unlucky day at the Freedom Tower. The young team of Southwest Sentinels was making use of the Wraith's training simulator when Kismet popped in to try and rob the place. Her charmed magics were simply too much for the team, and with the Freedom Five out foiling one of Baron Blade's plots, they called on the guardians of Megalopolis' sister city for help. The Dark Watch arrived only to find that Kismet had broken her way into Meredith Stinson's lab, and her jinxes were all supercharged! How could the heroes prevail when they kept hitting each other?!

The Sentinels, Dark Watch Setback, Nightmist, Dark Watch Mister Fixer, and Dark Watch Expatriette defeated Kismet in the Freedom Tower. I admit I chose the 5th hero and the variants judiciously - my plan was to get out the Caliginous Form immediately (SUPER USEFUL!!! - especially when Mission Control gave DW Fixer Alternating Tiger Claw) and I determined the other variants thinking that Fixer and Expatriette would get off fewer, but bigger hits.

The battle started quite poorly. Kismet's opening turn involved two Karmic Disjunctions, each of which revealed at least 4 Jinxes. So, thanks to the Talisman, her damage output increased ludicrously. Couple that with terrible opening hands on the part of Setback, Nightmist, and Mister Fixer, and I knew I was in for trouble.

The first few turns were a slog. While I did play the Caliginous Form on the first turn, three of the Sentinels got almost immediately incapacitated. Mission Control was the first Room to appear and it played an inappropriate Mists of Time that swapped Nightmist's 2-card trash with her all-the-cards deck, stalling her card draw further. About the only bit of luck was that Expatriette's opening weapon was a Submachine Gun, which specifically aims at Non-Hero targets, and she had Hollow Points in hand.

Then Kismet's luck began to turn around with, appropriately enough, Surprising Fortune. Setback accelerated Nightmist's card draw and she was able to put on her Amulet and thoroughly lock down Kismet's deck with three Mistbounds in a row. Mister Fixer started laying on a reliable beat-down, and the Sentinels brought out a number of cards that aim for Villain targets. Or they gave Mister Fixer Dark Delusions - whatever worked!

In the end, I got this challenge on the first try, though I reallllllly did not think that would be the case!

Pretty well, actually.  Started hairy, but soon, everything went under control.  PWAA 12, CC 10, PWF 12, H 17, PWT 15. 

 

The Vengeful Five kidnapped a schoolbus full of children to try and draw out the Freedom Five. 

Which would have worked if they hadn't had one of the Prime Wardens onboard the bus.

When they opened the hold of the Mobile Defense Platform, they found an enraged Haka with a gaggle of schoolchildren behind him.  "Intruders" came the call from the bridge, the remaining Prime Wardens responding to their compatriot's call for aid.  Haka chanted a ward over the children and their conveyence, and waded into the fray against Fright Train, while Captain Cosmc and PW Argent Adept made sure none of the children left the protective field.

Fanatic's anger got the better of her, and she laid waste to everything, friend and foe alike (Thanks, turn 3 EoD from PW Power), following up with throwing a Battalion Brute into Fright Train, knocking him senseless.  Argent Adept handed out card plays like candy (and actual candy to the children, to Haka's chagrin), while Captain Cosmic aided his friends greatly with Dynamic Syphons, Wounding Buffers and Energy Bracers.

Tempest's Otherworldly Resiliance, augmented by AA's shielding, allowed him to shrug off a large amount of attacks, while keeping his friends healthy.

While Haka took our Ermine, the Baron's serum got the better of him, and Haka used the baron as an object lesson for the children: Don't do drugs!

Proletariat and Friction were then taken out by Tempest on his last turn.
